children: What happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after Nvidia shares pulled back from the previous session's rally amid lingering corporate governance concerns and warnings of continued scrutiny.

CNBC reported that Nvidia shares tumbled around 7%, paring gains after soaring more than 30% in the previous session following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. According to the report, other U.S. semiconductor stocks also opened lower after strong previous-session gains, with Micron and AMD plunging 10% and Marvell Technology and Arm Holdings tumbling 8% in morning trading.

Analysts warned that scrutiny of Nvidia would continue, the report said. Strategy Asset Managers CEO Tom Hulick told CNBC that Nvidia still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance.

When a dominant industry leader pulls back after a sharp rebound, investors often reassess valuations and governance risks across related stocks. Share prices across a sector frequently decline together when doubts about customer spending and sector catalysts persist.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Semiconductor manufacturing company Camtek fell 4.1%.
Semiconductor manufacturing company MKS fell 7.6%.
Semiconductor manufacturing company POET Technologies fell 9.4%.
Semiconductor manufacturing company Ultra Clean Holdings fell 11.7%.
Analog semiconductors company NXP Semiconductors fell 5.4%. Is now the time to buy NXP Semiconductors?

children: Zooming in on Ultra Clean Holdings

Ultra Clean Holdings’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 96 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Ultra Clean Holdings and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 14% on the news that AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom. Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.

Ultra Clean Holdings is up 31.6% since the beginning of the year, but at $35.96 per share, it is still trading 74.8% below its 52-week high of $142.59 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Ultra Clean Holdings’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $628.54.
